settings.text:
Cotton sheets get softer with use when they are washed gently and dried with a little patience. Here is what helps.

General guidance. This is general advice for caring for cotton, cotton satin and polyester fills. It is not specific to one product. Always follow the care label on your item first.

settings.heading: Washing
settings.text:
• Wash new sheets and pillow covers once before you use them.
  • Wash with similar colours. Strong shades and two-tone sets are best washed on their own for the first few washes.
  • Use a mild detergent and a cool or warm wash, around 30 to 40°C, unless the label says otherwise.
  • Avoid bleach. It weakens cotton and can fade colour.
  • Leave room in the drum so the sheets can move and rinse properly.

settings.heading: Drying
settings.text:
• Line dry in the shade where you can. Strong sun can fade colour over time.
  • If you use a dryer, choose a low heat and take the sheets out while they are still very slightly damp.
  • Shake each piece out and smooth it by hand to keep creases down.

settings.heading: Ironing
settings.text:
• Cotton satin: if you iron, use a low to medium setting on the reverse to protect the sheen.
  • Quilted and embossed fabric: we suggest not ironing, as heat and pressure can flatten a raised pattern.

settings.heading: Storing
settings.text:
• Store sheets clean and completely dry.
  • Fold them loosely and keep them in a cool, dry cupboard, away from damp walls.
  • A cotton bag or pillowcase lets fabric breathe better than plastic.

settings.heading: Care label: Quilted Bed Sheet Set
settings.text: These are the care instructions given for our Quilted Bed Sheet Set. Other products may differ, so check each label.

settings.question: How often should I wash my sheets?
settings.answer: Many people wash sheets once a week, or more often in hot weather. Pillow covers can be washed more often, as they are closest to skin and hair.

settings.question: How do I treat a stain?
settings.answer: Act quickly. Blot, do not rub, then rinse from the back with cool water. Try a little mild detergent on the spot before a normal wash, and check the stain has gone before drying, as heat can set it.

settings.question: Why do sheets pill?
settings.answer: Pilling usually comes from friction. Washing with rough items such as towels or jeans makes it worse. Wash sheets with similar fabrics, use a gentle cycle and avoid over-drying.
